text:
Buffalo spent two periods being the better team and trailing by two goals anyway, then spent the rest of the night collecting what the chances had been promising. Danila Yurov scored on a power play slap shot and Maxim Shabanov added a snap shot 1:45 later, both in the second period, on shots that carried a 6 and 11 percent chance of going in. Minnesota took a 2-0 lead on 1.35 expected goals through two periods, a lead the play never really earned.

The third period turned it. Noah Ostlund deflected one in at 3:55 off passes from Owen Power and Rasmus Dahlin, and Tage Thompson tied it at 9:38 with a snap shot, his ninth shot on goal of the night. The Sabres generated 1.54 expected goals in that period against 0.27 for Minnesota. Jesper Wallstedt kept the Wild in it for a while, stopping 25 of 28 and saving 1.18 goals more than the quality of the chances would suggest, but the pressure was too heavy to hold off for 60 minutes.

Overtime belonged to the same side. Power, who logged 29:06 and was on the ice for 2.46 expected goals for against 0.70 against, beat Wallstedt with a wrist shot at 4:22 for a 3-2 win. Buffalo outshot Minnesota 64 attempts to 48 and won 83 percent of simulated replays of every shot, so the win fit the way the game was played. Minnesota got 2 goals from 1.98 expected, which is just about what its chances were worth. Only the two-goal head start was borrowed.
